content_units: 12-Week Data Analysis Path Snapshot

You have   72 total study hours   over 12 weeks, so the best path is the one that gets you to a job-ready portfolio fastest without overloading fundamentals. For   junior analyst roles in Toronto  , employers commonly ask for   Excel + SQL + BI/dashboarding  , with Python often listed as a bonus rather than a strict requirement.
Context used:
-   6 hours/week
-   Basic spreadsheet familiarity already
- Goal:   junior analyst employability
- Target market:   Toronto, Canada
Toronto-Focused Path Comparison
Path   Speed to job-ready output   Employability for junior analyst roles   Difficulty at 6 hrs/week   Best strengths   Main drawback

Excel + SQL + Tableau     Fast       High       Moderate     Strong business reporting; SQL is highly marketable; dashboards showcase well   Tableau is useful, but Power BI may appear more often in some local postings
Python + pandas + matplotlib   Medium-Slow   Medium-High     High     Strong long-term upside; great for automation and deeper analysis   Harder to become visibly job-ready in only 72 hours

Excel + Power BI + basic statistics     Fastest       Very High       Low-Moderate     Closest to many entry-level BI/analyst workflows; Power BI is widely requested; stats helps interviews   Weaker on SQL unless added later, and SQL is a big hiring signal
Best Choice for Your Goal
Best overall balance: Path 3 — Excel + Power BI + basic statistics
Why it wins for your priorities:
-   Speed:   You can build presentable dashboards quickly.
-   Employability:   Strong fit for many junior analyst and reporting analyst postings.
-   Difficulty:   More manageable than Python-heavy study while working full time.
-   Interview readiness:   Basic statistics helps you explain trends, averages, distributions, and business findings.
Close second
Path 1 — Excel + SQL + Tableau   is the strongest alternative if you want a slightly more technical profile.
If Toronto postings you target lean heavily toward   SQL  , this path may outperform Path 3 in pure hiring value.
Not best for 12 weeks

Path 2 — Python + pandas + matplotlib   is excellent long term, but with only 6 hours/week it is the hardest path to convert into fast employability. It is better as a   phase 2 upgrade   after landing the core analyst stack.
Recommended Ranking
Option 1:   Excel + Power BI + basic statistics     Fastest route to portfolio-ready analyst work and strong entry-level fit     Best balance
Learn Power BI
Option 2:   Excel + SQL + Tableau     Stronger technical signaling than Path 3, especially because SQL is highly valued     Best technical trade-off
Start SQL
Option 3:   Python + pandas + matplotlib     Best long-term analytics foundation, but slower and harder within 12 weeks     Best future upside
Learn pandas
12-Week Study Plan for the Best Path
If you choose   Path 3  , use the 72 hours like this:
Phase   Goal   Key Tasks   Deliverable
Weeks 1-2   Excel refresh   formulas; lookups; pivots; cleaning; charts   1 cleaned spreadsheet + summary sheet
Weeks 3-5   Power BI core   import data; model basics; visuals; filters; DAX basics   1 dashboard with KPIs and slicers
Weeks 6-7   Statistics basics   mean/median; variance; distributions; correlation; sampling   short analysis notes on 1 dataset
Weeks 8-9   Applied projects   sales/reporting case; HR or operations case   2 portfolio projects
Weeks 10-11   Portfolio polish   write insights; improve visuals; publish/dashboard screenshots   portfolio-ready case studies
Week 12   Job targeting   resume bullets; mock interview answers; apply to roles   tailored resume + applications
Why Path 3 Beats Path 1 for You

Path 1 is very strong, but   Tableau vs Power BI   is the key difference. In many business environments, especially for entry-level reporting and analyst work,   Power BI often gives more direct practical alignment  . Since you only have 12 weeks, that immediate alignment matters.
Still, Path 1 has one major edge:
-   SQL is more valuable than basic statistics   in many analyst job screens.
So the practical interpretation is:
- If you want the   safest quick-start path  : choose   Path 3
- If you can tolerate slightly more difficulty for better technical signaling: choose   Path 1
- If you want the   best long-term path  , not the fastest hiring path: choose   Path 2
Smart Hybrid for the Strongest Outcome
If you want the best real-world result, use this adjusted version of Path 3:
-   Excel
-   Power BI
-   Basic statistics
-   Light SQL in the final 2-3 weeks
That hybrid is likely stronger than any pure path listed because it preserves:
- the   speed   of Path 3
- the   market value   of SQL from Path 1
- a manageable workload for someone working full time
